method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: Options now compare relevant post-thyroid assessment domains. Neuromuscular symptoms plus calcium results most directly address the suspected biochemical complication; thyroid-specific reference is present.
Fresh blood/repeated swallowing requires prompt bleeding response regardless of vomiting. Cold-fluid or irritation normalization alternatives no longer depend on a red-treat giveaway.
New cooler pulseless foot after vascular surgery requires urgent perfusion escalation. Rest-based recheck cannot delay action; vascular-surgery reference is now topic-relevant.
Correct the visible external kink promptly and reassess rather than replacing, adding intake or forcing irrigation. Nephrostomy-specific source now supports the device context.
Secure partial displacement and obtain urgent team review; dressing-only or remaining urine flow cannot establish safe position. Appropriate nephrostomy reference is present.
New dusky stoma warrants surgical perfusion assessment. Larger opening may require fit review but does not justify delayed reassessment of possible ischaemia.

Nasogastric type is explicit and changed marking warrants holding use and approved position verification. Independently opened NG source supports marks for migration recognition and no use before verification.
Nasogastric initial confirmation is explicit; whoosh testing is not reliable proof. Independently checked NHS safety guidance and BCcampus NG source reject air testing as confirmation.

Two-day tract makes early dislodgement context clear; urgent expert guidance is appropriate and blind catheter/tube insertion is unsafe. Item does not generalize this restriction to all mature tract plans.

Narrow metabolic/fluid objective makes electrolytes and balance/oedema the appropriate SATA keys. Delivered calories or enjoyed meals do not directly detect these complications; NICE monitoring guidance supports content.
New symptomatic phosphate fall after refeeding prompts team review rather than calorie escalation or deconditioning attribution. The item does not independently prescribe a replacement regimen.

New unilateral respiratory changes after central access require urgent complication assessment while imaging is arranged. Analgesic response cannot rule out complication; central-line-specific reference now present.

Pale/cool/painful hand under radial compression requires urgent perfusion assessment and access-protocol response. Radial-specific reference replaces generic wound source; no independent arbitrary pressure setting is prescribed.
Expanding groin swelling with dizziness needs bleeding response and circulation assessment; marking alone cannot justify waiting. Arterial-access reference now matches topic.
Clinical content is acceptable, but current ref still c-postoperative wound healing. Regional block recovery/assistance source remains required; general anaesthesia alone is not adequate.
